source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party analyst commentary (not confirmed as AR's own wording): 'Navin Fluorine benefits from rising preference for Indian fluorochemical suppliers amid China+1 sentiment, which advantages NFIL's export-led business'; another summary noted NFIL is 'investing in capacity... drawn by the China+1 shift.' Could not verify explicit AR-text framing or revenue attribution.

inr_exposure.evidence: Quarterly (not full-year) export figures cited by brokers: exports were ~57% of revenue in Q1FY25 and ~77% in Q4FY25 — too inconsistent/quarter-specific to use as a reliable full-year export % without reading the AR segment note directly.

pli_scheme.evidence: Not listed among named beneficiaries of the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs (Dr Reddy's, Cipla, Glenmark, Biocon, Wockhardt cited as primary beneficiaries); one summary stated NFIL is expanding capacity 'without direct PLI support.'

rural.evidence: Broker/company commentary: 'APL Apollo has grown much faster in rural areas, expanding its base in rural markets,' with value-added products 'strengthening its presence in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities.' No explicit rural revenue % disclosed in a source read directly.

govt_capex.evidence: Sector commentary: 'domestic demand expected to rise by 9%-11% YoY, driven by sustained government infrastructure spending on roads, railways and ports'; 'PMAY-Gramin extended to FY29, targeting 2 crore additional rural houses' (structural tubes used for roofing/frames). A Q1FY26 investor-presentation-derived breakdown cited by a broker showed 'infrastructure' as 10% of volume/revenue mix (building material housing 67%, commercial 19%, others 4%) — cited for context but not confirmed as FY24-25 AR figures.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are HR coils, galvanized coils and zinc (steel-linked, not crude-oil-linked): 'HR coil prices being market linked... exposing the company to volatility in raw material prices which impacts profitability margins.' Not a crude-oil-exposure story.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to ~30 countries via SEZ-based Bhuj plant and a Dubai facility ('Bhuj facility's SEZ location enables export-competitive pricing for Middle East and African markets'), but no export-revenue % or hedging policy was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: APL Apollo is not named among the ~27 companies that signed MoUs under the Specialty Steel PLI scheme in available Ministry of Steel-related coverage; one generic sector note said the segment is 'expanding on the back of... PLI scheme support' without confirming APL Apollo's own participation.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Uses cash-flow hedges against forex exposure; per broker commentary, 'Effective FY26, realized cash flow hedge gains/losses are reclassified from revenue to forex gain/loss within other income/expense to align with peer practice and isolating revenue and EBIT margins from forex movements, with PBT and PAT unchanged.'
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 geography split cited by brokers: Americas ~53.9% of revenue, EMEA ~34.7% (together ~88.6%), implying the great majority of revenue is USD/GBP/EUR-denominated versus a small India/APAC residual. Full India-specific domestic % not confirmed from a primary source.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/industry commentary (not confirmed verbatim from the AR itself): 'Divi's plays in well as a China+1 strategy for major pharma companies as they look to de-leverage from dependence on Chinese API manufacturers... As U.S. and European firms push to diversify away from China, Divi's proven expertise positions it as a key beneficiary.' Separately, the company's own commentary on FY23-24 destocking referenced 'raw-material diversification away from China' (input-sourcing side, not customer-order side).

crude_exposure.evidence: General industry-level note only (not Divi's-specific disclosure): pharmaceutical API/intermediate synthesis broadly relies on petrochemical-derived feedstocks; no Divi's-specific raw-material-cost-to-crude linkage percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue-from-operations by geography (broker/press summary of results): Europe Rs 5,192 cr (56.46%, up from 52.3% in FY24), North America Rs 1,488 cr (16.18%, down from 17.1% in FY24), India Rs 1,105 cr (12.02%), Asia Rs 1,044 cr (11.35%), RoW Rs 367 cr (3.99%); overall 'Divi's Laboratories maintains a diversified global presence, with 88% of its sales revenue derived from exports in FY25.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Divi's Laboratories does not appear on the Feb-2021 list of companies approved under the PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs (approved firms cited: Natural Biogenex, Symbiotec Pharmalab, Macleods, Optimus Drugs, Sudarshan Pharma, Saraca Labs, Emmennar Pharma, Hindys Lab, Aarti Speciality Chemicals, Meghmani, Sadhana Nitro Chem).

govt_capex.evidence: Company is empanelled under Ayushman Bharat/PM-JAY and CGHS government health schemes, and incurred capex of INR 6,449 million during the year (incl. INR 1,367 million for the Mumbai hospital) mainly for bed-capacity expansion and the Noida project; no revenue % tied to govt capex was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International patient revenue rose 17% YoY in Q4FY25 to ₹55.7 crore, contributing 6% to total revenue; Medical Value Travel (MVT) revenues were reported at ₹539 crore in FY25 (source: Business Standard/Medical Buyer coverage of Q4FY25 results, not the AR text itself).

china_plus_one.evidence: DGTR issued final findings (June 2026) recommending anti-dumping duty on TPU-based Paint Protection Film imports from China, which the company — as a domestic TPU PPF manufacturer — is expected to benefit from; this is a trade-protection/import-substitution angle rather than an explicit customer-diversification China+1 narrative in the MD&A itself (source: search snippets, AR text not directly read).

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported zero net debt and cash reserves of ₹650 crore as of March 31, 2025, suggesting low overall interest-rate sensitivity, but no floating-rate liability % was disclosed in sources reviewed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Major raw materials (PTA & MEG) are crude-oil derivatives with volatile pricing; company mitigates via forward contracts and long-term agreements, and manufactures polyester chips in-house to reduce reliance on outside vendors. No raw-material cost % of revenue was disclosed in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company has a price pass-on arrangement plus a hedging mechanism to safeguard margins against forex volatility; sizeable imports provide a natural hedge against exports, with the company partially hedging net unhedged exposure.
inr_exposure.evidence: "The company has in place an effective price pass-on arrangement as well as hedging mechanism to safeguard its margins against raw material price volatility and forex volatility... sizeable imports provide a natural hedge against the significant exports." Company derives maximum revenue from USA customers (no exact % disclosed in sources reviewed).

rural.evidence: "GSK Pharma's established distribution network covers urban and rural areas... broad distribution footprint in urban and semi-urban regions" (from a brokerage stock note on GSK Pharma, not the AR itself); no revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: "India contributed 40% of revenues while the US formulation business accounted for 47% of consolidated revenues in FY24"; Q1 FY26 update shows US revenues at 49% of consolidated revenues, indicating continued high USD-linked revenue share (source: search snippets/press coverage, not the AR text directly).

govt_capex.evidence: Company's 'Vision 2031' strategy cites 'deepening presence in strategic end-markets (defense, engineering, railways, real estate)' as a growth pillar — implies exposure to government/infrastructure-linked steel demand, but no revenue % is disclosed in sources reviewed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Capex is 'funded entirely through internal accruals, with debt to equity capped at 0.5x' (conservative leverage, debt-to-equity ~9-20% per aggregator data); floating-vs-fixed rate debt split not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: 'Shyam Metalics Flat Products has been selected to invest under the production linked incentive (PLI) scheme for specialty steel,' among qualifiers alongside Tata Steel, JSW Steel, JSPL, AMNS India and SAIL (Business Standard, on the Rs 6,322-crore PLI scheme for speciality steel).

inr_exposure.evidence: 'Exports contributing 88.4% of total revenue' of FY26 turnover (₹57,167 million); company operates across 47 countries with revenue concentrated in Americas, Europe, Asia Pacific and Middle East & Africa banking clients (exact USD-specific % and formal hedging policy text not located in sources reviewed).

china_plus_one.evidence: Company management (investor presentation commentary) stated 'active projects are shifting from larger CRDMO players in China to Sai Life Sciences in India,' and that the 'BIOSECURE Act acts as an accelerator for a trend that began post-COVID' of pharma diversifying away from China; CEO: 'the long-term fundamentals of innovation-led outsourcing and supply chain diversification continue to remain strong, and we are well positioned to participate meaningfully in this opportunity.'

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company 'uses derivative financial instruments or other hedging techniques to cover potential exposure to foreign currency risks'; near-total revenue is USD/EUR-denominated against an INR cost base, giving partial/imperfect natural hedge (a strengthening rupee compresses margins).
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Exports account for 99% of total revenues, primarily from the US and Europe.'

pli_scheme.evidence: Government PLI incentives are cited as one of several positive structural factors for India's CRDMO industry broadly (alongside skilled-chemist availability and cost structure), but no Sai Life Sciences-specific PLI benefit or revenue linkage was confirmed in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company is distinguished by its 'China-plus-one' strategy, having built a supply chain with minimal dependence on Chinese raw materials; management told Moneycontrol it is now 'the second source for many products made in China, and the first choice for new ones' — cited as a driver of revenue CAGR of 24.8% and ~30% EBITDA growth over the last five fiscal years.

inr_exposure.evidence: 'Approximately 80% of revenue comes from Europe and North America'; separately reported that 'more than half of Anthem revenue comes from US, followed by Europe, India' — implying majority USD/EUR-denominated revenue against an INR cost base, though exact currency-exposure % and formal hedging policy text were not located in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: 'Anthem Biosciences Pvt. Ltd. is listed as a beneficiary under the [government] PLI scheme, with financial assistance being provided for creation of common infrastructure facilities in Bulk Drug Parks' (PLI Bulk Drugs scheme beneficiary listing).

rural.evidence: Search summaries of FY25 commentary note revenue driven by 'increased volumes, organic expansion, and strong performance in Tier-III and Tier-IV towns,' and management guidance to pursue 'deeper penetration in Tier 2/3 cities' and 'scale-up of franchise collection centres' (no exact revenue % disclosed in sources reviewed).

china_plus_one.evidence: Company describes a 'balanced manufacturing and outsourcing' model (in-house ~60% / outsourced ~40%, with export product sourced 76% from India and 24% from China) framed by management as a way to 'be a lean organisation as well as de-risk against cost escalations, currency fluctuations and other headwinds'; also expanding footprint into Chile, Vietnam and Cambodia. No explicit 'China+1' framing with direct revenue attribution found in a primary-source AR excerpt.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Reported as not using formal hedging/derivative contracts; relies on ability to reprice goods at in-country warehouses and on natural hedges where local currencies are USD-pegged/USD-denominated.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'The company has not gone for any hedging and does not enter into derivatives contracts... their currency risk management in warehoused locations involves the ability to increase the price of goods in the warehouse to offset losses caused by currency risk on receivables... Some of the countries where the company operates use the US dollar as their local currency, which provides a natural hedge.' FY25 disclosure cited: forex earned ~INR 720 Cr vs forex used ~INR 25 Cr (exports vs imports).

china_plus_one.evidence: Glenmark's API subsidiary Glenmark Life Sciences (GLS) — the entity historically positioned as a China+1 beneficiary — had its majority stake divested by the parent (deal concluding around FY24), reducing the current consolidated (parent) entity's direct exposure to an API/China+1 growth narrative going into FY24-25. No China+1 framing found for the current consolidated formulations-led business in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: 'Glenmark Pharmaceuticals Limited was approved as a domestic company in Group A of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme' for bulk drugs/APIs (government PLI scheme for KSMs/drug intermediates/APIs). Note: this approval predates/relates to the API business since majority-divested into Glenmark Life Sciences, so current parent-level revenue benefit is unclear (revenue_pct not disclosed in sources reviewed).

china_plus_one.evidence: Third-party industry research (not Kajaria's own AR text) notes anti-dumping duties imposed by the US/Europe/GCC on Chinese ceramic tiles have shifted some global demand toward India's Morbi export cluster, and that Morbi-based exporters focusing on international markets 'innately reduc[es] competitive intensity and price wars' domestically for organised players like Kajaria. This is an indirect/industry-level dynamic, not a company-specific China+1 attribution found in a primary Kajaria AR excerpt, so not scored as a genuine company narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Industry-wide (not Kajaria-specific) commentary indicates natural gas and other energy inputs can represent roughly 22-35% of total ceramic tile production costs, and that gas-price/supply disruptions have historically pressured sector margins; no Kajaria-specific FY24-25 percentage was found in sources reviewed (note: exposure is primarily to natural gas/fuel, not crude oil directly).

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 total revenue of ~INR 7,896 crore split as domestic INR 3,660 crore (46.4%) vs international INR 4,236 crore (53.6%), with international further split into Emerging Markets INR 1,510cr, Europe INR 1,474cr, Canada INR 1,252cr (per Q4FY25 results commentary) — no single 'USD revenue %' or hedging policy disclosure was located via search.

china_plus_one.evidence: "Uno Minda set a goal in 2023 to double export revenues as a buffer from fluctuations domestically. The company set up dedicated export lines in its plants and opened customer-facing offices in key regions (Europe, ASEAN...), ensuring products met local certifications and allowing Uno Minda to build direct relationships with global OEMs" (IBEF 'Success Story: Uno Minda's Export Journey'); management also cited targeting mid-teens export growth FY26-28 driven by lighting/acoustics shipments to Europe and ASEAN. No explicit 'China+1' framing tying this to customer diversification away from China was found.

pli_scheme.evidence: "Uno Minda is one of five auto component makers likely to receive incentives under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme from FY27 onwards, along with Dana TM4 India, Varroc Engineering, Napino Auto, and Cummins Technologies India" (Business Standard, 'Eight more companies to get incentives under auto PLI from FY27: MHI'). Incentives had not yet begun flowing as of FY24-25, so no revenue % is disclosed.

rural.evidence: "Radico Khaitan sees tier-2 cities, white spirits driving next phase of alcohol demand" — company/analyst commentary identifies expanding market opportunities in tier-II cities as a driver of premium spirits growth (multiple secondary sources, no specific revenue % disclosed).

crude_exposure.evidence: Secondary commentary notes packaging/logistics cost pressure linked to crude oil and rupee moves: "surging crude oil prices and a weaker rupee are increasing import costs for packaging and other inputs, with glass bottles up about 20%, paper cartons nearly 100%, and logistics costs up roughly 10%" — company's core raw material is ENA/molasses (largely self-supplied via 160 million litre distillation capacity), with glass/packaging carrying indirect crude-linked cost exposure. No % of raw material cost tied to crude was disclosed in a primary source located.

china_plus_one.evidence: Petronet LNG is a domestic LNG import/regasification and gas-marketing company (Dahej and Kochi terminals, plus the upcoming Gopalpur terminal) selling exclusively into the Indian market; no export business or China+1 supply-chain narrative found.

govt_capex.evidence: Kochi terminal utilization has historically been constrained by pipeline connectivity; utilization (record ~29% in a recent period vs Dahej's ~94%) is expected to rise once GAIL's national-grid pipeline connectivity (e.g., Bangalore pipeline, targeted by June 2026) is completed — Petronet's volumes are partly dependent on government/GAIL-owned pipeline infrastructure buildout rather than Petronet's own government-linked revenue share.

crude_exposure.evidence: Petronet's long-term LNG supply contract (originally RasGas, now QatarEnergy, extended 2028-2048 for 7.5 MMTPA) is priced on an oil-linked formula — historically tied to the trailing 12-month Japan Crude Cocktail (JCC) with caps/floors, and the newer extension reported at roughly a 12% slope to crude oil — meaning LNG procurement cost (the company's dominant input cost) moves directly with crude oil prices. No specific 'raw material as % of revenue' figure was located in a primary source.

inr_exposure.evidence: LNG is procured under USD-denominated, crude-linked long-term contracts; a Business Standard headline on Q2 FY26 results referenced an 'FX loss' impacting results ('Petronet Q2: Analysts upbeat on long-term outlook despite FX loss, UoP hit'), consistent with material USD-denominated purchase costs, but no explicit hedging policy or USD revenue % was found in a primary source.
